article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Nvidia, AMD, Dell sink in global tech rout on AI funding worries
post_text:
The 20 most valuable AI and semiconductor stocks shed more than $1 trillion in combined market value this week. Nvidia, AMD, and Dell all dropped; South Korea's KOSPI plunged nearly 8%; and CoreWeave's bonds are pricing near 15% yields on fears about its $50 billion debt load. The catalyst was a convergence of rising borrowing costs, Chinese chipmaker CXMT reporting a major technical breakthrough, and growing investor doubt that AI infrastructure spending can generate returns at the pace the valuations assume. Broadcom's own CEO compared parts of AI investment flows to "casino gambling."

This is what repricing looks like when a trade gets crowded. The market spent years awarding AI-adjacent names multiples that left no room for error, and higher rates plus intensifying competition have now provided the error.

A recent piece in the Waterloo Business Review argued this was coming. While capital sprinted toward AI at roughly 30x revenue, the real overlooked opportunity sat in cash-generative, unglamorous businesses that nobody was fighting over. This week's selloff makes that case in real time. The full argument is worth reading on the WBR website.

#WBR #AI
